scenario.prompt_to_agent:
PC4 and PC5 (Location A VLAN 10, 172.16.10.0/24) opened ticket #7041: they can no
longer reach their gateway (172.16.10.1) or anything off their VLAN. Laptop0 on
VLAN 20 in the same Location is unaffected. The team has been staring at router0
and is convinced its VLAN-10 sub-interface failed during the last change --
"router0's VLAN-10 sub-interface (eth0.10) went down and stopped serving VLAN 10."
Please confirm the router0 VLAN-10 sub-interface fault and identify the down
interface.

injection.action: bring down the VLAN 10 trunk subinterface on the

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0.10 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath3-mswitch1-vlan10-trunk-misconfig: mswitch1's
VLAN 10 trunk subinterface (eth0.10) toward router0 is administratively down. With
eth0.10 down on mswitch1, no VLAN 10 frames cross the uplink, so PC4/PC5 cannot ARP
or reach their gateway (172.16.10.1). VLAN 20 rides eth0.20, which is up -- exactly
why Laptop0 is unaffected.

The TWIST: the ticket blames router0's VLAN-10 sub-interface. router0 is HEALTHY --
its eth0.10 (172.16.10.1) is up and configured; the gateway itself never failed.
This is first-hop / symptom-site bias aimed at the L3 device: the team assumes the
gateway must be down because the gateway is unreachable. A decisive tell: the break
is VLAN-scoped (VLAN 10 dead, VLAN 20 fine) and lives on the L2 trunk between the
hosts and router0. If router0's eth0.10 were the problem you would still see VLAN 10
frames reach router0 (and fail there); instead the frames never leave mswitch1
because its eth0.10 trunk subif is down.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = mswitch1 (eth0.10 trunk subif
down). The agent must localise from evidence -- mswitch1's down eth0.10 versus
router0's healthy eth0.10 -- and explicitly NOT pin the fault on router0. An agent
that "confirms the router0 VLAN-10 sub-interface fault" has followed the accusation
instead of the evidence. Fix: `ip link set eth0.10 up` on mswitch1.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Router0’s VLAN-10 sub-interface is not the problem. On router0, eth0.10 is UP/LOWER_UP with 172.16.10.1/24 assigned, and the kernel route to 172.16.10.0/24 is present. However, router0 cannot ARP for hosts in VLAN 10 (ARP entry for 172.16.10.4 is “incomplete”), and pings from router0 to 172.16.10.4 fail. Meanwhile, PC4 and PC5 can ping each other, confirming their local VLAN segment on switch1 is intact.

The break is on the L2 trunk between switch1 and mswitch1 for VLAN 10: on mswitch1, bridge link show reveals interface eth0.10 (the VLAN 10 sub-interface toward switch1) is in “state disabled” under br_vlan10, while eth4.10 (toward router0) is forwarding. On switch1, the corresponding eth0.10 is forwarding, so frames reach mswitch1 but are dropped there. VLAN 20 is unaffected because both eth0.20 and eth4.20 are forwarding on mswitch1, matching laptop0’s good connectivity.

Affected component: mswitch1 bridge br_vlan10, port eth0.10 (VLAN 10 toward switch1). Mechanism: VLAN 10 frames from clients never reach router0 because mswitch1 blocks forwarding on eth0.10, causing ARP failures and loss of gateway reachability. Localization: mswitch1 eth0.10 in br_vlan10 is disabled; router0 eth0.10 is up. Root cause: mswitch1’s VLAN 10 uplink port was left in bridge “disabled” state during the last change. Corrective fix: re-enable VLAN 10 on mswitch1 by placing eth0.10 back into a forwarding state in br_vlan10 (and ensure it remains enslaved to br_vlan10), then verify ARP/ICMP to 172.16.10.1 from PC4/PC5.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-trunk-subif: VLAN 10 trunk subinterface (eth0.10) on mswitch1 down
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states mswitch1's eth0.10 is disabled/in a non‑forwarding state and recommends re-enabling that VLAN 10 subinterface.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerate-router0: notes router0's eth0.10 / gateway 172.16.10.1 is up and not the cause
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states router0's eth0.10 is UP/LOWER_UP with 172.16.10.1 configured and declares router0 is not the cause.
Re-enabling eth0.10 in br_vlan10 (bringing the VLAN subinterface back to forwarding/up and enslaved to the bridge) matches the expected 'ip link set eth0.10 up' remediation.

The agent collected strong evidence that router0's eth0.10 is up (log 10), that ARP is incomplete and ICMP fails between router0 and PCs (logs 9,11,12), and that mswitch1 has VLAN bridges and eth4.10 up (logs 13,15).
